decision.summary: The kernel supplies the proposed inherited custody before mode userspace, with the same existing owner/GNU/mode. Permanently tracing GNU introduces a concrete timeout-delivery dependency on the owner. Detaching GNU while retaining the already attached mode removes that steady-state dependency, but no proved timer-ready/detach/release bootstrap exists in the supplied source. Accounting and event-state joins also require implementation. This is a specific incomplete route, not a Linux impossibility finding.

supported.finding: With the complete option mask installed by successful SEIZE before release of the exact owned launcher, GNU ordinary fork attaches the child during copy_process, copies current ptrace flags including SEIZED and EXITKILL, links it to the same tracer, and requests its initial stop before wake_up_new_task. The child is already in kernel custody before exec/interpreter Python can run. The GNU parent FORK event is emitted after wakeup: the child initial STOP may be reported first. Do not confuse initial STOP with proof that the parent event has already been consumed.
supported.boundary: All FORK/VFORK/CLONE classes must be enabled; CLONE_UNTRACED bypasses automatic tracing. This is adequate evidence for the pinned trusted ordinary GNU fork and existing permitted thread creation, not a hostile-code containment claim.

supported.finding: Owner exit walks its retained ptraced list under tasklist serialization and sends SIGKILL to every EXITKILL tracee before unlinking. This covers an auto-attached mode still in its initial stop or interpreter prefix when the owner dies at the original wall or root CPU endpoint. Fork and tracer-exit ordering is supported: if child linkage wins it is in that list; if tracer exit wins, GNU receives fatal SIGKILL and copy_process checks fatal_signal_pending before committing a new child. SIGKILL is not a signal-delivery-stop.
supported.limits: This is a source ordering argument, conditional on qualified actual timer/API delivery. Sending SIGKILL is not an observed terminal event, successful reap, lock closure, or final CPU receipt. GNU death alone does not trigger mode EXITKILL because its tracer is the owner; the retained owner deadline still supplies the original wall cutoff, and active cleanup must process GNU death.

supported.finding: A PTRACE_DETACH of GNU affects that exact task only. The mode already has a copied option word and its own link in the owner ptraced list, so detaching GNU does not remove mode EXITKILL or mode inherited tracing of later threads. After GNU is detached, GNU SIGALRM no longer requires owner CONT; its timeout handler can send genuine SIGKILL to the mode/group even while the owner is stopped. GNU still has the existing launcher PDEATHSIG binding for owner death.
supported.limit: Only supported after the child attachment has actually been established. Later GNU forks would not auto-attach; the pinned GNU source has one fork. This permission-free source conclusion does not supply a timer-ready handshake or authorize DETACH execution.

supported.finding: wait_task_zombie returns RUSAGE_BOTH to the tracer, but a reparented traced process leader goes EXIT_ZOMBIE -> EXIT_TRACE and does not credit tracer RUSAGE_CHILDREN. It is unlinked and reported to the real parent, which can then reap and accumulate its CPU. Only EXIT_DEAD leaders accumulate the process/thread and previously waited child CPU into the reaping parent. Thus final exclusive complete-tree RUSAGE_CHILDREN remains a supported authoritative total; raw tracer wait4 rows are not additive receipts.
